result.title: Unimodal Augmentation-based SSL Objectives Induce Cross-Modal Alignment
result.summary: Recent works have observed implicit cross-modal alignment between independently trained unimodal models. However, the mechanisms underlying the emergence of this phenomenon remain unresolved. In this paper, we demonstrate that unimodal augmentation-based self-supervised objectives implicitly induce cross-modal alignment. We show that low unimodal losses force high cross-modal alignment, whereas a high unimodal loss prevents such alignment. We theoretically connect the widely used InfoNCE loss to local CKA, the popular measure of cross-modal alignment. We further provide extensive empirical evidence supporting this claim, both in controlled settings and across 53 unconstrained frozen text, vision, and audio unimodal encoders. In both cases, unimodal augmentation-based objectives control cross-modal alignment. Overall, our results provide a theoretical and empirical foundation for understanding the emergence of implicit cross-modal alignment by establishing a direct connection between unimodal training objectives and cross-modal structure.

AI.brief_summary: 论文论证仅用单模态数据增强的自监督目标会隐式诱导跨模态对齐：理论上把 InfoNCE 损失与局部 CKA 这一常用对齐度量联系起来，说明单模态损失低则对齐强、损失高则难以对齐，并在受控设置和 53 个冻结的文本、视觉、音频编码器上给出经验支持。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以局部 CKA 与 InfoNCE 建立单模态训练目标与跨模态表示对齐的直接联系，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 推理状态是否保留并对齐视觉证据提供度量与理论线索。
